ruleStates.definition: The creation rule has reviewed structured authority, executable server validation, guided UI, evidence, and passing tests. Nothing about it requires GM memory, prose interpretation, or manual repair.

The rule is enforced and explained through the guided workflow, but part of its authority is an app-owned runtime derivation (code-derived) rather than a standalone catalog fact. Acceptable at final closure only when the derivation is catalog-bound with a source fingerprint.

The rule is deliberately variable per campaign. Its bounds are canonical; its value comes from the versioned policy. Complete when the policy field, bounds validation, editor control, and draft binding all exist.

The rule is validated but its violation is survivable table variation. It renders as a non-blocking warning with an explanation and never silently disappears. Final acceptance requires every warning to be intentional, not an unfinished error.

The rule cannot be implemented because structured authority is absent or ambiguous (open DATA-ONB defect) or an upstream contract is missing. A blocked rule cannot ship; final closure permits zero blocked rows.
The rule does not apply to the current workflow branch (e.g. milestone choices for a level-1 start, gender for genderless species). Must be derived structurally, never by hiding UI.

workflowBranchStates.definition: One Level 1 Trainer plus policy starter(s): the first playable vertical slice. Every rule row must be complete/guided/campaign-policy before P9-060.
Levels above 1 including milestone choices, larger budgets, and rank caps. Complete before P9-092.
Starter count above 1 with team composition and overflow. Complete before P9-050.
Adoption of pre-existing characters. Complete before P9-070.

acceptancePredicates: No hidden mandatory step: every decision required for a legal build is represented as an explicit guided decision with completion state.
No unresolved blocker: zero rules in blocked state and zero open DATA-ONB defects at closure.
No out-of-band repair: no workflow branch requires raw IDs, JSON editing, SQLite access, or ad hoc sheet repair to reach ready-for-play.
No client-downgraded severity: hard-rule violations render as blocking everywhere and are re-checked server-side at submit and approval.
No orphan option: every selectable option resolves to a stable canonical or policy ID that the server can re-authorize.
No silent not-applicable: branch exclusions derive from structured conditions recorded in the catalog.
